title: MIMOMamba: From Scalar Duality to Matrix-Valued Attention
claim: A sequential recurrent computation and a parallel matrix-masked attention computation are two dual views of the same underlying model.
layout: 2 rounded panels, left-to-right, bold double-headed arrow labeled duality between them
description: Two large rounded-rectangle panels joined by a thick double-headed black arrow labeled 'State Space Duality'. The left panel, 'Recurrent view (MIMO SSM)', shows a chain of three gray circular hidden states h_{t-1}, h_t, h_{t+1} connected by blue horizontal arrows labeled A_{t-1}, A_t. Red arrows labeled B feed inputs x upward into each state, and green arrows labeled C carry outputs y upward out of each state. The right panel, 'Parallel view (matrix-valued dual attention)', shows a stack of red cards labeled B_t as 'Block queries Q' and a stack of green cards labeled C_t as 'Block keys K'. Beside them is a lower-triangular 3x3 'Matrix-valued mask L' with identity blocks on the diagonal, blue A blocks below it, and gray blocks above it. The colors map each symbol across the two views.

abstract: The state space duality (SSD) framework, central to modern state-space models (SSMs) such as Mamba, has established an efficient attention-like mechanism by leveraging the commutative property of linear recurrences. However, existing formulations are limited to single-input single-output (SISO) systems that enforce commutativity with a restrictive scalar-identity constraint, which prevents cross-dimensional interactions within the state dynamics. In this work, we generalize SSD to the multi-input multi-output (MIMO) setting by introducing a matrix polynomial parameterization. This approach not only provides a principled way to ensure commutativity for generalized duality but also induces a shared algebraic structure across state transitions, thereby significantly reducing parameter redundancy. Building on this foundation, we present \textbf{MIMOMamba}, a multi-head SSM architecture that captures rich cross-dimensional dynamics while retaining linear-time training. Empirical evaluations on a sequence modeling benchmark demonstrate that MIMOMamba achieves performance comparable to or surpassing that of standard Transformers while utilizing substantially fewer parameters.
